title: Bromoviridae Coverage Audit
h1: Does the cucumber mosaic virus module actually work?
standfirst: Bromoviridae is a tripartite plant-virus family built at family level because all five genera share the layout: RNA1 carries 1a, RNA2 the RdRp and in the cucumoviruses 2b, RNA3 the movement protein and the coat protein. Cucumber mosaic virus, brome mosaic virus, alfalfa mosaic virus, tobacco streak virus. This module was measured for the first time here and a real defect came out of it.

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Tripartite, so one genome arrives as three records and must be merged.

blocks.html: Every BV-BRC record carries contigs=1, so a genome is deposited as three separate records sharing a name and merge_segments.py is mandatory at annotation time.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: The naming trap: the source calls two different proteins “replicase”.

blocks.html: 1a and 2a are different proteins on different segments, and the source calls both replicase. That string is therefore not binned on the word at all — it is routed to REP1 or REP2 by length against the two measured medians, and anything far below either is left unbinned rather than assigned to whichever is nearer.
§08 is about what happened when that routing was given no margin.

sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit
sections.lede: 400 for 1a, 300 for the RdRp, 80 for the structural proteins.

blocks.html: REP2's max_len was 993 aa and is now 900. The old value was exactly REP1's median length, which is the whole of §08 in one number.

sections.title: Does it route?
sections.lede: 69.5% — the honest figure, and it is not the one first reported.

blocks.html: An earlier measurement reported 94.8%. That used --merge-by-name, which collapses records sharing a genome name — intended for the segments of one multipartite genome, but it also merges independent isolates deposited under one name, counting several genomes as one. The unmerged figure is 69.5%.

A three-way split is documented and has not been acted on: Cucumovirus alone routes 94.0%, Ilarvirus 71.0%, and the Alfamovirus group 100%. Splitting would improve every genus, as it did for Carlavirus and Quinvirinae.
69.5% routed. The family is held together by shared gene layout, but its routing would be better served by three modules.

P2B is the cucumovirus 2b silencing suppressor and is genuinely absent from the other genera, so its 50% is biology and it correctly carries no copy_num. Every assignment in the shipped module was already right.

sections.title: Are the calls right?
sections.lede: 89.2% genuinely clean — after the fix in §08. Before it, 43.9%.

blocks.html: The duplicate-call audit is now completely empty: no exact duplicates, no nested calls.
30.5% of the family does not route on 25 references, and the documented three-way split that would fix it has not been done.
No mature peptides. Neither 1a nor 2a has cleavage sites documented for this family in a form that can be located from the sequence.
The evaluation is a sample — 148 genomes at ≥6 kb, seed 29. Routing in §04 is a census.

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: Two profiles calling one gene, on a third of all genomes.

blocks.html: REP1 and REP2 were called on identical coordinates in 32% of genomes. They are 1a and 2a — different proteins on different segments — so sharing coordinates is not merely suspicious, it is impossible.

blocks.text:
REP2 collection   n=590   median 840 aa   max 993 aa
REP1 collection   n=293   median 993 aa   min 908 aa

3 of REP2's 590 members hit REP1 at 97% identity / 100% coverage
REP2 max_len was 993 -- exactly REP1's median length

blocks.html: Three 1a sequences had been binned into the REP2 collection. They formed their own cluster, produced their own profile, and that profile fired on 1a — and REP2's length window, whose ceiling was exactly REP1's median, admitted the call. The module's own build notes warn that the source calls both proteins “replicase”; the length routing that was supposed to separate them had no margin at the top.

Removing the three sequences, rebuilding REP2 (587 sequences, 29 profiles) and tightening max_len to 900 took the module from 43.9% to 89.2% genuinely clean and eliminated the duplicate calls entirely.
Fixed. Three contaminating sequences and one length ceiling, worth 45 points of genome quality.

The module's vocabulary is complete after two genomes. The source reaches 49 distinct strings with its knee at 132 and is still climbing — and among those strings is the bare word replicase standing for two different proteins, which is what §08 is ultimately about.
